name: Lamb/mutton
anchor: per-commodity sovereign metallic-contamination schedules for terrestrial animal foods — Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule (the only credible instrument on the register with a complete meat, poultry and egg panel), EU Regulation (EU) 2023/915 for cadmium in muscle meat, and FSANZ Schedule 19 for lead in muscle meat; canned forms additionally carry the canned-foods tin maximum level, and the plant-protein analogue row reads across from EU and Hong Kong pulse, soy and cereal commodity maximum levels
native_basis_label: as sold, raw or cooked edible portion (wet weight); bone and inedible fat excluded; no dry-to-wet or reconstitution conversion is performed
scope_note: Muscle meat and attached edible fat of domestic sheep (Ovis aries) at any age: lamb, hogget and mutton, in fresh, chilled, frozen, ground/minced, primal and sub-primal, and plain cooked forms with no added non-meat ingredients. Goat (Capra hircus) is covered by the same sovereign rows, which enumerate goat alongside sheep, and is certified on this row. Ovine and caprine edible offal is a separately-tested sub-lot against the sovereign offal maximum levels and never anchors this row. Merguez, lamb sausage and other formulated products route to the processed-meats row; canned mutton routes to the canned-meats row; wild sheep and goat species route to the game-meats row.
basis_guard: (wet weight|portion ordinarily consumed|product as placed on market|food as listed|as sold|as consumed|commodity|edible part|fresh weight)
basis_guard_note: Category 11 is a dietary as-sold wet-weight category. The guard admits only register rows whose basis is a food-matrix content basis (wet weight, portion ordinarily consumed, product as placed on market, commodity, edible part, food as listed in the Cap 132V schedule). It rejects, by construction, food-contact specific-migration limits, toy and article element-migration limits, animal-feed 12%-moisture bases, dry-matter fertiliser limits, colour-additive ingredient purity specifications, and drinking-water statutory limits. A migration or purity-specification number is not a maximum level for a food and must never anchor a meat, poultry, or egg row.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only initial setting: the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for this exact product form in its native basis; disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated; control where neither a sovereign number nor a supportable near-neighbour analogue exists; never occurrence-derived)

Pb.label: strictest applicable sovereign muscle-meat lead maximum level; FSANZ Schedule 19 and Hong Kong Cap. 132V agree at 100 ug/kg
Pb.substantiation: Two credible sovereign instruments regulate this exact cell and agree: FSANZ Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code Schedule 19 sets 0.1 mg/kg for meat of cattle, sheep, pig and poultry excluding offal, and Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 sets 0.1 mg/kg for meat of cattle, pig, goat and sheep. The corresponding EU Regulation (EU) 2023/915 and Codex CXS 193-1995 muscle-meat lead rows are ABSENT from this register and are therefore not named and not assigned a value from memory; they are recorded as register gaps for ingestion through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway. Because Method v2.0 selects the strictest applicable value, ingesting them can only lower this cell or leave it unchanged, never raise it, and this cell must be re-derived when they land. The looser edible-offal lead maximum levels (Hong Kong 0.15-0.20 mg/kg, FSANZ 0.5 mg/kg) are a DIFFERENT product scope and are deliberately not used to anchor this muscle-meat row: Ovine offal is a separately-tested sub-lot governed by the offal maximum levels of its own species. BASIS OF THE BINDING INSTRUMENT, DISCLOSED: the two concurring instruments are written on DIFFERENT bases. FSANZ Schedule 19 states its maximum level for the portion ordinarily consumed (an as-consumed basis); Hong Kong Cap. 132V states the identical 0.1 mg/kg as-sold, for the edible portion after removal of bones and fat (Cap. 132V Part 2 Note 1). Because this row publishes an as-sold ceiling, the Hong Kong as-sold row is named as the binding instrument and the FSANZ row is disclosed as an independent sovereign value concurring at the same number. The published ceiling therefore rests on an instrument written in this row's own basis, and no as-consumed value is relabelled as-sold. The number is unaffected: both instruments sit at 100 ug/kg, so the strictest-applicable selection is identical either way.

Cd.label: strictest applicable sovereign muscle-meat cadmium maximum level; EU 2023/915 and Hong Kong Cap. 132V agree at 50 ug/kg
Cd.substantiation: EU Regulation (EU) 2023/915 Annex I sets 0.050 mg/kg cadmium for meat of bovine animals, sheep, pig and poultry, expressly excluding offal, and Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 sets the same 0.05 mg/kg for meat of cattle, pigs, goat and sheep. Cadmium concentrates in liver and kidney, and the sovereign liver (0.5 mg/kg) and kidney (1.0 mg/kg) maximum levels are an order of magnitude looser; they govern offal sub-lots and are deliberately not permitted to anchor this muscle-meat row.

tAs.label: Hong Kong Cap. 132V total-arsenic maximum level for meat of animal
tAs.substantiation: Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule sets 0.5 mg/kg arsenic (expressed as total arsenic) for meat of animal, the edible portion after removal of bone. Hong Kong was admitted to the HMTc credible-regulator set on 2026-08-17 precisely because its per-commodity metallic-contamination schedule covers terrestrial-animal commodities that the EU, Codex and FSANZ leave open. No credible sovereign government sets a stricter total-arsenic maximum level for terrestrial muscle meat. The toxic inorganic fraction is separately controlled under the iAs cell, which is a control with reflex speciation rather than a not-material determination.

iAs.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for terrestrial red-meat muscle tissue. Every credible inorganic-arsenic instrument on the register is scoped elsewhere: EU 2023/915 and EU 2025/1891 to rice, rice products, fruit juices, infant food and seafood; UK, Health Canada and US FDA to rice-based and juice matrices; Hong Kong Cap. 132V to rice and aquatic animals. A NOT-MATERIAL determination is deliberately REJECTED for this cell rather than adopted for convenience: organoarsenical feed additives (roxarsone, nitarsone, arsanilic acid, carbarsone) were lawfully administered to poultry and swine in major producing markets within living memory and are documented to leave arsenic residues in edible tissue, so the programme will not make the affirmative claim that no inorganic-arsenic pathway exists in terrestrial animal food. For the ruminant rows, where no equivalent additive history applies, the absence of that pathway does not by itself substantiate a not-material determination either, because neither a sovereign number nor a supportable near-neighbour analogue exists for the cell in any case. Because no sovereign number governs the cell and no near-neighbour cell is a supportable analogue (a rice or seafood inorganic-arsenic maximum level describes a different contamination mechanism entirely), the cell is a control: testing is mandatory and no ceiling is invented.
iAs.reference_method: Inorganic arsenic by anion-exchange HPLC-ICP-MS speciation. Speciation is reflex-triggered on every lot whose total-arsenic screen is quantifiable above the method limit of quantitation, and unconditionally on the first lot from any new supplier, slaughter establishment, or country of origin. Any quantifiable inorganic arsenic is escalated to the certification committee together with the feed-additive and origin declaration; the lot cannot be released on an inorganic-arsenic result while the escalation is open, and a total-arsenic result at or above the binding total-arsenic maximum level is a hard stop irrespective of speciation.

tHg.label: Hong Kong Cap. 132V total-mercury maximum level for meat of animal
tHg.substantiation: Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 item for mercury (expressed as total mercury), meat of animal, 0.05 mg/kg = 50 ug/kg. This is the same instrument and the same row that anchors the Category 35 bone-broth mercury cell, adopted on the 2026-08-17 credible-set ruling. The EU, Codex and FSANZ set mercury maximum levels only for fish and seafood, so Hong Kong supplies the only credible terrestrial-animal mercury ceiling and it binds directly rather than by read-across.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic sediment and biomagnifies through aquatic food webs. Terrestrial red meat carries no methylation pathway and no aquatic trophic transfer, and methylmercury is in any event a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), so it is bounded by and controlled through the published total-mercury cell (50 ug/kg total mercury, Hong Kong Cap. 132V). No separate methylmercury ceiling is published because none would bind below the total-mercury ceiling and none is set by any credible sovereign government for this product form.
MeHg.reference_method: Not measured routinely. Bounded by the total-mercury cell; methylmercury speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS is reflex-triggered only where a lot's total-mercury result approaches the binding total-mercury maximum level, or where the formulation incorporates a fish, fish-meal, or marine-derived ingredient, which would additionally route the lot to the Category 6 seafood mercury ceilings.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury content limit for meat, poultry, game, eggs, or meat analogues. The credible methylmercury instruments (EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.3, US FDA CPG 540.600, FSANZ Schedule 19, Hong Kong Cap. 132V) are scoped exclusively to fish, crustaceans, molluscs and other aquatic animals. Methylmercury is a species of, and arithmetically bounded by, total mercury.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Regulation (EU) 2023/915 Annex I); UK retained contaminants law; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (CPG 540.600); FSANZ Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada; Hong Kong Cap. 132V Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations Part 2 Schedule — none sets a methylmercury limit for a terrestrial animal food, an egg, or a plant-protein meat analogue.

Ni.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a nickel maximum level for meat of cattle, pig, goat, sheep or any other terrestrial mammal. The EU nickel maximum levels recorded on the register (the eu2024_ni_* family) are drawn exclusively over plant matrices — cereals, pulses, legume, leafy and root vegetables, tree nuts, oilseeds, cocoa — and the only other credible nickel values are drinking-water statutory limits and a food-contact specific-migration limit, both in bases that cannot govern the content of a food. A plant-commodity nickel maximum level is not a supportable near-neighbour for animal muscle tissue, which accumulates nickel by a different route and at a different order of magnitude, so no read-across is available and no ceiling is invented.
Ni.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on every certified lot, trended per SKU and per production line. Escalation is triggered by a result above the SKU's established rolling upper control limit, or by an increasing trend across three consecutive lots, and directs the investigation to nickel-bearing stainless contact surfaces (grinders, mincers, brine injectors, forming plates). No numeric ceiling is published because no sovereign instrument compels one.

Sn.rationale: Inorganic tin in food is a tinplate-packaging pathway: tin migrates into the food from the internal surface of an unlacquered or damaged tinplate can, which is why every credible sovereign tin maximum level on the register is written against canned food rather than against the food itself. Fresh, chilled, frozen and vacuum- or modified-atmosphere-packed red meat is not packed in tinplate, so the pathway that the canned-food maximum levels exist to control is absent and no sovereign number governs the cell. A lot of this product form that is retorted or packed in a metal can is not certified against this row at all: it is certified against the canned-meats row, whose tin cell carries the binding canned-foods maximum level. No tin ceiling is invented for the non-canned form.
Sn.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Any quantifiable tin in a lot declared as non-metal-packed triggers a packaging and contact-surface investigation (can or closure liner, tinned equipment, solder) before release, and re-routes the lot to the canned-meats row if metal packaging is found.

companions.scope: canned foods other than canned beverages, except canned dried and canned

Al.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an aluminium maximum level for meat, poultry, game or eggs. The credible aluminium values on the register are drinking- and bottled-water statutory limits (EU 2020/2184, US FDA 21 CFR 165.110, Health Canada), a food-contact specific-migration limit (EU 10/2011), toy element-migration limits, and the FSANZ Schedule 19 aluminium maximum levels for infant formula. None can anchor this row: the water and migration values are in a different basis, and an adult food must not borrow an infant-formula maximum level (products marketed for ages 0-5 route to Category 1 by the taxonomy boundary rule). No read-across is supportable and no ceiling is invented.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, trended per SKU. Escalation is triggered by a result above the SKU's established rolling upper control limit or by an increasing trend across three consecutive lots, and directs the investigation to aluminium contact surfaces and packaging (foil, trays, aluminium cookware, aluminium-containing processing aids). No numeric ceiling is published because no sovereign instrument compels one.

Cr.screen_note: Total chromium in food is dominated by benign trivalent chromium, an essential trace element; the health-relevant species is hexavalent chromium, which does not persist in this matrix (see the Cr-VI cell). The Hong Kong Cap. 132V total-chromium maximum level is a real sovereign limit and is published here, but it is recorded as a SCREEN: it is a contact-surface and equipment-leaching tripwire, not a standalone protective ceiling, and it is excluded from the firm-limit count.
Cr.label: Hong Kong Cap. 132V total-chromium maximum level for meat of animal, published as a screen
Cr.substantiation: Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule sets 1 mg/kg chromium for meat of animal. It is the only credible sovereign total-chromium value for a terrestrial-animal food and is adopted at face value, but recorded as a screen because total chromium is not the health-relevant analyte: the toxic species is Cr(VI), which does not persist in a reducing protein matrix (see the Cr-VI cell).

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is not stable in this matrix. Raw and cooked red-meat muscle tissue is a wet, reducing, protein- and thiol-rich medium; Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III) by tissue reductants (cysteine, glutathione, ascorbate) and by the acid and heat of digestion and cooking, so a Cr(VI) figure reported on such a matrix is an artifact of the extraction chemistry of the total-chromium screen rather than a measurement of a species that persists in the food. The determination follows the same reference-method adjudication recorded for the hexavalent-chromium cell in the infant-formula category (data/workbench standards Cr-VI adjudication), applied here to an animal-tissue matrix. Hexavalent chromium is in any event a species of, and bounded by, the published total-chromium screen (Cr-VI <= total Cr).
Cr-VI.reference_method: Not measured routinely. Bounded by the total-chromium screen (Cr cell). Alkaline-extraction Cr(VI) determination (IC-ICP-MS) is reflex-triggered only where the total-chromium screen exceeds the published screen value, in which case the investigation is directed at stainless-steel contact surfaces, grinders, and brine or marinade equipment rather than at the raw material.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign government sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for any food. Every credible Cr(VI) instrument on the register is an article, textile, leather, toy-migration, tattoo-ink, fertiliser or electrical-equipment limit in a non-food basis, and applying one to a food matrix would be a basis conflation the compiler's basis guard rejects. Total chromium is regulated for meat and poultry by Hong Kong Cap. 132V and is published here as a screen.
Cr-VI.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Regulation (EU) 2023/915; Regulation (EU) 10/2011; Directive 2009/48/EC; REACH restrictions); UK; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA; FSANZ Schedule 19; Health Canada; Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule — none sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for food.
